clue.text: Motorway exit for Pet, ticoat Lane

parts.note: a slip is a woman's petticoat worn under a dress
a lane is a narrow road

explanation.surface: Directions to a motorway turn-off for a famous London street market.
explanation.walkthrough: Petticoat Lane is a well-known Sunday street market in east London, so the surface reads as a place name rather than two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip road is the short access ramp by which traffic leaves or joins a motorway.

clue.text: Tell tales about a silly little girl

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second here

parts.note: to tell tales is to lie
a silly, used as a noun, is a fool or ass

explanation.surface: Someone accuses a foolish young girl of telling tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassie is the Scottish and northern word for a young girl.

clue.text: Quiet nobleman is a real jewel

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
an earl is a British nobleman

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken aristocrat is praised as a treasure of a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively a gem of a person or thing, something of great worth, is a pearl.

clue.text: Sent photo to be developed there and then

indicators.note: film that is developed is processed and changed, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A picture is sent off to the lab for processing immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be developed' rearranges the nine letters of SENT PHOTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms for immediately and at the very place where something happens.

clue.text: Translator makes venison producer consume fish

indicators.note: consume means the first piece eats, so takes in, the second

parts.note: venison is the meat of deer
cod is a common fish

explanation.surface: A translator is portrayed as making a deer eat fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoder renders a coded message into plain language, a kind of translation.

clue.text: Expel advocate from underworld's drinking haunt

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
a bar is a place to drink

explanation.surface: A lawyer is thrown out of a gangland pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To disbar is to strike a barrister off, expelling them from the legal profession.

clue.text: Fiendish fellow holds me back

indicators.note: holds means the first piece contains the second

parts.note: a don is a university fellow

indicators.note: back means the word me is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a wicked man is restraining them.
explanation.definitionFit: Demon used before a noun means fiercely or devilishly energetic, as fiendish can.

clue.text: Doesn't her work need to be condensed?

indicators.note: to work something is to shape it, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A question whether a woman's writing ought to be cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges the letters of DOESNT HER, the apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Condensed and shortened both mean made briefer.

clue.text: A man housed man from the States

indicators.note: housed means the first piece gives a home to the second

parts.note: taken as the word man itself
Eric is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man has given lodging to a visitor from the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: American is the adjective for someone or something from the United States.

clue.text: A viewpoint expressed obliquely

parts.note: a slant is a particular point of view or angle on a matter

explanation.surface: An opinion is put across indirectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslant means at a slope or angle, slantwise.

clue.text: Habitual hesitation by non-scholarship student

parts.note: common means usual or habitual
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A student without a scholarship keeps pausing as they speak.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and some other universities, a commoner is an undergraduate who holds no scholarship or exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: The university term for an undergraduate paying their own way, without an award.

clue.text: Account form for the Chief Constable

parts.note: the Bill (the Old Bill) is British slang for the police
a head is a chief

explanation.surface: A form is set aside for the senior police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chief Constable is the head of the Bill, the police in British slang, so the clue's two words give the pieces in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: A billhead is a printed heading on an invoice, or the sheet carrying it, used for accounts.

clue.text: A fool can suffer set back with humour

indicators.note: set back means the word for can is read in reverse

parts.note: a tin is a can
wit is humour

explanation.surface: A fool can take a setback with good humour.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a fool taking a setback well; 'suffer' sits between the can and its reversal indicator only to make that picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a silly or stupid person.

clue.text: Go crazy-involved with government bureau

parts.note: to go is to depart
mental is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Getting mixed up with a ministry drives someone mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Departmental means relating to a department, a section of government.

clue.text: Discards dried fruit when making a pancake

parts.note: to drop is to discard
a cone is the dry woody fruit of a conifer

explanation.surface: Raisins are thrown out while preparing a griddle cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop scone is a small thick griddle cake, also called a Scotch pancake.

clue.text: Mark is generous, despite apprehension

parts.note: m is an abbreviation for mark, an old German currency
giving means generous

explanation.surface: Mark is open-handed in spite of his doubts.
explanation.definitionFit: Misgiving is a feeling of doubt or worry about the outcome.

clue.text: "Deploy more reps!" they rule

indicators.note: to deploy is to arrange or position, so these letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Sales bosses demand more representatives in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deploy' rearranges the letters of MORE REPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Emperors are sovereigns who reign over empires.

clue.text: Memorialist sadly died, but was celebrated ever after

indicators.note: sadly here signals that the word memorialist is put into disorder

explanation.surface: A writer of memorials dies but is remembered for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges MEMORIALIST into IMMORTALISE, then D is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To immortalise is to make famous or remembered for all time.

clue.text: Indian city enjoying good fortune at present

parts.note: luck is good fortune
now means at present

explanation.surface: An Indian city is currently having a lucky streak.
explanation.walkthrough: Lucknow is the capital of the state of Uttar Pradesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucknow is a large city in northern India.

clue.text: Order issued last month about food-additive code

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December, the last month of the year
re means about or concerning
E is the prefix of the codes for food additives, E numbers

explanation.surface: A ruling was published last month on labelling food additives.
explanation.walkthrough: In Europe, approved food additives carry codes beginning with E, called E numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree is an official order or edict.

clue.text: Vet is heartened by Irish poetry

indicators.note: heartened by here means the middle of vet is is replaced by a new centre

parts.note: Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland

explanation.surface: An Irish poem gives a veterinary surgeon fresh heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartened by' means given a new heart: keep only the first and last letters of 'Vet is' and put the Irish language between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Verses are lines or stanzas of poetry.

clue.text: Sounds like the only capital in SE Asia

indicators.note: sounds like signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: sole means only

explanation.surface: A claim that a certain city is the one capital in South-East Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Seoul is the capital of South Korea, in east Asia.

clue.text: Embrace Edward for having sewn up the deal

parts.note: a clinch is a close embrace
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A hug for Edward after he secures the agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To clinch a deal is to settle it conclusively, to sew it up.

clue.text: Arrest army men for taking dried coconut

parts.note: to cop is slang for to arrest
RA is the Royal Artillery, a corps of the British army

explanation.surface: Soldiers are detained for stealing coconut.
explanation.definitionFit: Copra is the dried kernel of the coconut, pressed for oil.

clue.text: Visit London and throw caution to the winds

explanation.surface: Someone heads to the capital and lets their hair down.
explanation.definitionFit: Town in British speech often means London, so a trip there is one sense; the idiom also means to act lavishly or with abandon.

clue.text: Report that one has not been excluded

definitions.text: that one has not been excluded

explanation.surface: An account says that someone was included after all.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a pun: split as I'M PART it says that one is a part, not left out.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart is to make known or communicate; split differently it declares being included.

clue.text: A fine fellow, too

parts.note: a swell is a fashionable gentleman

explanation.surface: A good chap is mentioned in addition.
explanation.definitionFit: As well means also or in addition.

clue.text: Rebuke manufacturer of hairpieces

parts.note: a wig is a hairpiece, and to wig someone is to rebuke them, so the maker of the one is pictured as a maker of scoldings

explanation.walkthrough: To wig, or give a wigging, is British slang for a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who makes wigs and toupees for customers.
